sourceBoundary: Targeted recent oncology surveillance across FDA, EMA and indexed ClinicalTrials.gov mirrors; direct NIH API and record-history retrieval blocked. Verified primary FDA and EMA listings but no newly distinct reportable oncology decisions in this scan. International registry surveillance is not exhaustive. All trial-level status and result details are flagged as registry-derived and require reconciliation before treatment or enrollment decisions.

studies.name: IOV-PED-101
studies.cancer: Relapsed/refractory pediatric, adolescent and young-adult solid tumors: rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, primary CNS malignancies, melanoma, soft tissue sarcoma
studies.molecularEligibility: No specific somatic mutation required; resectable tumor tissue for autologous TIL manufacturing and residual measurable disease required
studies.geography: Five study sites, United States (Colorado, Florida, New Jersey, New York)
studies.finding: Registry-derived change Oct 16: active/not recruiting to terminated. Actual enrollment 5 versus former estimate 40. Study completion revised from July 2028 (estimated) to June 19, 2026 (actual). Sponsor states it chose to end all remaining participant visits after reviewing available safety and efficacy data.
studies.limitations: Sponsor did not attribute the decision specifically to a safety event; no causal adverse-event signal, negative efficacy result, or implication for other Iovance protocols can be concluded. Status is confirmed in multiple independently indexed mirrors, not directly through NIH API.

studies.name: DIT309 Phase 1
studies.cancer: Advanced osteosarcoma or soft tissue sarcoma after standard therapy
studies.molecularEligibility: Tumor tissue must express protocol-defined target antigen; antigen identity and positivity threshold not stated publicly
institutions: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine (collaborator)
studies.finding: Registry-derived status changed Oct 14 from recruiting to suspended. Listed reason is 'Data update in progress.' Planned enrollment 15.
studies.limitations: Do not infer a safety hold or failed efficacy; suspension reason is administrative/unspecified. Public record has inconsistent age text (display >=8 years, inclusion criterion >=8 weeks), requiring primary registry reconciliation.

studies.name: NKTR-255 after CD19 CAR-T (18-255-01)
studies.cancer: Adult relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
studies.molecularEligibility: No named somatic mutation required; prior labeled CD19-directed CAR-T with axicabtagene ciloleucel or lisocabtagene maraleucel
studies.biomarker: CD19 is the CAR-T target; it is not a tumor-genetic eligibility mutation
interventions: NKTR-255 interleukin-15 receptor agonist after CD19-directed CAR-T
institutions: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis
University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
studies.geography: United States; multicenter with study locations in multiple states
studies.status: TERMINATED before 2026-10-16; Oct 16 event is RESULTS_POSTED, not a new termination
studies.finding: Trial results posted Oct 16 for 15 participants in Stage 1 (11 received various NKTR-255 doses, 4 placebo); none entered Stage 2. Month-6 complete-response counts were 8 combined NKTR-255 versus 2 placebo. Study had already ended by sponsor decision and is recorded as terminated.
studies.limitations: Very small, terminated dose-escalating study; counts alone do not demonstrate comparative efficacy, statistical significance or Phase 3 success. Registry-reported results accessed through mirror, not via direct NIH API.
